prompt: A company buys a scanner, adds it to the pipeline as a job allowed to fail, and a month later nobody reads its output. What did not change?

choices.text: Who acts on a finding, and when
choices.why: Right. The tool ran; the routine around its findings stayed the same, so nothing reached anybody.

choices.text: The number of checks the pipeline runs
choices.why: It runs one more check than before. The count changed and nothing else did.

choices.text: The licence the company holds for its tools
choices.why: Buying the scanner changed exactly that, and it is the cheap part.

choices.text: How long the pipeline takes on each push
choices.why: A scanner job adds minutes, so the duration did change.

prompt: In the arrangement where security is a phase, how does a finding reach the developer who wrote the code?

choices.text: As a failing stage in the build of their own change
choices.why: That is the DevSecOps arrangement, which this one is contrasted with.

choices.text: As a report, then a ticket, after the release
choices.why: Right: a report in a different place, after the context is gone.

choices.text: Through the pre-commit hook on their laptop
choices.why: A hook is a pipeline practice; the phase model has no check on the laptop.

choices.text: It does not reach them; the security team fixes it
choices.why: The security team reviews; the fix still lands on whoever the ticket goes to.

prompt: The pipeline passed. In a DevSecOps team, what does that pass assert?

choices.text: The service has no security defects left anywhere in its code
choices.why: A pipeline finds what its checks have rules for. A design flaw passes every one of them.

choices.text: A security engineer read the change
choices.why: Nobody read it. The pass is about the checks, which is why it scales.

choices.text: The agreed checks ran and passed, or were excepted on record
choices.why: Right. The answer to "did anybody look?" is a written list, every time.

choices.text: The scanners found nothing at all
choices.why: A finding that was excepted with a reason does not stop a pass.

prompt: Put the stages of linkbox's pipeline as the course ends it in the order they run: the first four.
On Tuesday the composition analysis reports an advisory with no fixed version. Why does the build pass with a warning instead of breaking?

choices.text: Advisories without a fix are not real vulnerabilities
choices.why: They are real. The question is who can act on one, and today nobody on the team can.

choices.text: Nobody on the team has a fix
choices.why: Right. A build that breaks for what nobody can fix stops everybody's work and teaches them to bypass it.

choices.text: Warnings are for dependencies, breaks for code
choices.why: The rule is about whether a fix exists, not about where the finding is.

choices.text: The security champion approved the build by hand
choices.why: Nobody approved it by hand; the gate decided by its rule, and the champion read the advisory afterwards.

prompt: A token was pushed to the shared repository an hour ago. What comes first?

choices.text: Deleting the line in a new commit
choices.why: The token stays in the history and in every clone. Deleting it first leaves it working.

choices.text: Rewriting the history
choices.why: Clones made in that hour still have it; the rewrite is a later step.

choices.text: Asking who cloned the repository in that hour
choices.why: You cannot know every copy, which is the reason the token has to stop working.

choices.text: Revoking the token, so the copies open nothing
choices.why: Right. A pushed secret is burned; making it worthless is the step that does not depend on finding the copies.

prompt: Match each role to what changes in its week.

pairs.right: fixes what the pipeline finds in their own change, before merge
triages what is not obvious and keeps exceptions honest
chooses and tunes the checks and writes custom rules
handles a new advisory for something already running

right_distractors: reviews every release by hand before it ships

prompt: A finding was raised three weeks ago and nobody has answered it: not fixed, not excepted, not marked false. What is the cost the lesson names?

choices.text: The finding expires and the scanner stops raising it
choices.why: A finding has no expiry of its own; an exception does, and there is none here.

choices.text: The team learns to ignore the pipeline
choices.why: Right. An unanswered finding is how a check stops being read.

choices.text: The build breaks for every later change
choices.why: Whether it breaks depends on the gate's rule, not on its age.

choices.text: The security team is told automatically
choices.why: Nothing in this pipeline escalates by age; that is what the champion's Friday look is for.

prompt: Why does the course recommend running the lab on your own computer rather than online?

choices.text: Online machines cannot run Docker or any container at all
choices.why: A Codespace runs Docker; the online path works.

choices.text: The scanners refuse to run in a cloud
choices.why: Nothing in the course checks where it runs.

choices.text: Docker runs natively there, as in every transcript
choices.why: Right, and the online path depends on one company's free allowance besides.

choices.text: It is the only path that needs no account
choices.why: The virtual machine needs no account either.

prompt: `docker version` answers for the client but the server part fails with `permission denied` on the default socket. What does `id -nG` tell you?

choices.text: Whether you are in the docker group now
choices.why: Right. Missing, or added since the last login: both give that error.

choices.text: Which version of the daemon is running
choices.why: `id` knows users and groups, nothing about Docker's version.

choices.text: Whether DOCKER_HOST points to another socket
choices.why: That is `echo $DOCKER_HOST`; this error names the default socket.

choices.text: Whether the daemon has stopped running
choices.why: A stopped daemon gives a different message, about the socket not answering.

prompt: After downloading uv's release and its checksum file, the command that compares the two is: sha256sum ___
linkbox's tests replace `app.DATABASE` with a file in a temporary directory. What would go wrong if they used `linkbox.db` instead?

choices.text: SQLite refuses two connections to the same file
choices.why: SQLite accepts them; the trouble is what the rows already there do to the assertions.

choices.text: They would see each other's links
choices.why: Right. A search test would find links another test made, and a run would depend on the one before it.

choices.text: Flask needs the path to be absolute
choices.why: A relative path works; the app uses one when it runs.

choices.text: The file is ignored by git, so pytest cannot see it
choices.why: pytest opens files on disk whatever git tracks.

prompt: The lesson says linkbox carries at least four security defects and asks you to leave them. Which one is visible to anybody who can read `settings.py`?

choices.text: The search builds its SQL from the text typed
choices.why: That one is in `app.py`, in the search route.

choices.text: The dependencies are pinned to old versions
choices.why: They are in `requirements.txt`.

choices.text: The administration token is written in the file
choices.why: Right. Whoever reads the repository has the token, and lesson 6 deals with it.

choices.text: Flask's debug server is started with debug on
choices.why: That is the last two lines of `app.py`.

prompt: How many packages did `uv pip install` put in the virtual environment for linkbox and its tests?
The two requirements files pin nine packages between them, and the install put thirteen in the environment. Where did the other four come from?

choices.text: Dependencies of the pinned ones, which the files never name
choices.why: Right: `packaging`, `pluggy`, `iniconfig` and `pygments`. Lessons 13 and 15 come back to what that means.

choices.text: uv adds its own helpers to every environment it makes
choices.why: uv lives outside the environment, in `~/.local/bin`, and adds nothing to it.

choices.text: pip and setuptools, which every virtual environment carries
choices.why: uv's environments have neither unless asked, and neither is in the list it printed.

choices.text: Older versions kept beside the pinned ones
choices.why: One version of each package is installed, the pinned one.

prompt: In this lab, where does the list of stages a push runs live?

choices.text: In the post-receive hook on the server
choices.why: The hook only checks out the commit and starts that commit's own pipeline.

choices.text: In `ci/stages`, inside the repository
choices.why: Right. A change to the list travels with the commit and is reviewed like code.

choices.text: In `~/ci/runs`, beside the logs
choices.why: That directory holds what each run did, after the fact.

choices.text: In git's configuration for the remote `ci`
choices.why: The remote is only an address to push to.

prompt: Why does the hook clone the pushed commit into a new directory for every run instead of reusing one checkout?

choices.text: git refuses to check out into a directory that exists
choices.why: git checks out into existing repositories all the time.

choices.text: A clone is faster than a checkout
choices.why: It is slower; the hook pays that for something else.

choices.text: So an old run cannot pass it
choices.why: Right. A virtual environment or a file from yesterday's run would make today's result depend on yesterday.

choices.text: Docker needs a fresh build context each time
choices.why: Docker builds from any directory, fresh or not.

prompt: Put what happens after `git push ci main` in order.
items: git updates main in the bare repository
the post-receive hook reads the old commit, the new one and the branch
the hook clones the new commit into ~/ci/runs/N/src
ci/pipeline.sh runs each stage in ci/stages
the last line says whether the pipeline passed

prompt: A repository with no working files, the kind a server holds, is created with: git init ___ ~/ci/linkbox.git
You push, git prints `To /home/ana/ci/linkbox.git` and the branch moves, and there are no `remote:` lines. What does that mean?

choices.text: The pipeline passed so quickly it printed nothing
choices.why: A pipeline that runs prints a line per stage and a last line; silence means it did not run.

choices.text: The push was refused and git rolled it back
choices.why: The branch moved; a refused push says so and moves nothing.

choices.text: Nothing checked the commit
choices.why: Right. A hook that is not executable is skipped with only a hint, and the push still succeeds.

choices.text: Docker is not running, so the stages were skipped
choices.why: A stage that cannot reach Docker fails and says so in the run's output.

prompt: Match each message to its cause.

pairs.left: failed to connect to the docker API at unix:///run/nothing.sock
pairs.right: DOCKER_HOST points at a socket nothing listens on
another process already listens on the port
the package index could not be reached

right_distractors: a requirement names a version that does not exist

prompt: A command fails. You run it again with nothing changed, and it fails with a different message. What does the lesson say that tells you?

choices.text: The tool has a bug and should be reinstalled
choices.why: Reinstalling changes the machine before you know what changed it.

choices.text: Something on the machine changed between the two runs
choices.why: Right, and finding what changed comes before anything else.

choices.text: The second message is the real one and the first can be ignored
choices.why: Both are information; the difference between them is the clue.

choices.text: The error is intermittent and the command should be retried until it passes
choices.why: A pass after retries hides whatever changed.

prompt: Which of these are part of the lab this lesson builds? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: a bare repository whose hook runs the pipeline
choices.why: Yes: ~/ci/linkbox.git.

choices.text: a registry on localhost:5000
choices.why: Not yet: lesson 8 starts it.

choices.text: a directory per run with its checkout and logs
choices.why: Yes: ~/ci/runs/N.

choices.text: a kind cluster
choices.why: Not yet: lesson 10 creates it.

choices.text: uv, installed from its release with the checksum checked
choices.why: Yes, in ~/.local/bin.

prompt: A teammate proposes moving the pipeline's stage list from `ci/stages` into the server's hook, "so nobody can weaken it in a commit". What does the move cost?

choices.text: Nothing: the hook runs the same stages either way
choices.why: It runs the same stages until the day they differ for one branch and nobody can see why.

choices.text: The checks would stop being reviewed with the code
choices.why: Right. The list in the repository is reviewed in the same change; the hook is edited by whoever has the server. Lesson 16 protects the list a different way.

choices.text: The hook would run slower because it reads a longer file each time
choices.why: Reading a list takes no measurable time either way.

choices.text: git refuses hooks longer than a few lines
choices.why: git runs a hook of any length.
